generated_output.summary: Google Maps (or similar Google system packages like com.google.android.apps.maps) is not visible in running processes or app listings due to package filtering rules or how system processes/applications are categorized and filtered in ProtectionManager or AppModelFilter.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: ProtectionManager includes a specific toggle/group for google packages (`googleEnabled`) which checks if packages start with `com.google.android.`; if this group is disabled or if filtering logic excludes system/Google packages, applications like Google Maps do not appear.

step_by_step_plan.description: Write a unit test verifying that Google Maps (com.google.android.apps.maps) remains visible in app listings and protection groups, then run the test command to validate.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Android categorizes apps into user apps and system apps, often grouping pre-installed or vendor apps under specific namespaces like com.google.android.*.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Understanding how package namespaces and system flags work ensures tools can correctly locate and display pre-installed applications without hiding them accidentally.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Google Maps is a pre-installed system/Google application whose visibility depends on how package filters handle Google namespaces.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The app queries running processes via shell commands like dumpsys and ps and maps them back to Android package names.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: If process name matching or regex filtering fails to match a package's process name format, the application will fail to list it as running.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Google Maps processes might be filtered out or not matched correctly by the process loader utility.

common_pitfalls: Modifying global app filters without accounting for user preference toggles.
Hardcoding package names instead of relying on proper namespace or system flags.
